summary.en: The government lifted the state of emergency in four regions, while ethnic violence erupted in Wau town and clashes in Lakes State left seven dead. SPLM officials in Western Equatoria dismissed reports of an attack on the chairperson-elect's residence, and gunmen opened fire on a Juba-Mundri vehicle, injuring two passengers. Women and girls continue to face severe gaps in support, with survivors of gender-based violence lacking essential services, and a rape victim walked four hours for medical care. The country is pursuing a trade and investment hub role and has partnered with Israel's Gilat to launch nationwide satellite internet. 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Regjeringen opphevet unntaketilstanden i fire regioner, mens etnisk vold brøt ut i Wau-byen og kamper i Lakes State førte til syv døde. SPLM-tjenestemenn i Western Equatoria avfeide rapporter om et angrep på den nyvalgte lederen sin bolig, og væpnede åpnet ild mot et kjøretøy på Juba-Mundri-ruten, og såret to passasjerer. Kvinner og jenter fortsetter å møte store mangler i støtten, med overlevende av kjønnsbasert vold uten nødvendige tjenester, og en voldtatt kvinne gikk fire timer for å få medisinsk hjelp. Landet forfølger en rolle som handel‑ og investeringsknutepunkt og har inngått samarbeid med Israels Gilat for å lansere satellitinternett i hele landet. 2 dødsfall knyttet til kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
